summary: Checks whether a value is the `NaN` number.
description: Nothing is coerced first, which is where this differs from the global `isNaN`: that one converts its argument, so `isNaN("abc")` and `isNaN(undefined)` both report `true`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is the `NaN` number; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isNaN(NaN); // => true
isNaN(0 / 0); // => true
isNaN(0); // => false
isNaN("abc"); // => false
isNaN(undefined); // => false
```
